title: FOMC Introductory Statement, September 16, 2026
summary: Fed chair announces a rate hike: the economy and labor market are strong but inflation has run above target for over five years with no improvement in underlying trends.

assertions.quote: for more than 5 years, inflation has been running above target
While uncertainty remains elevated owing in part to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient.
This summer's inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.
Unemployment claims on a four-week moving average are running at levels consistent with full employment.
Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the committee's 2% goal.

verdicts.note: Tighter policy restrains demand and anchors expectations, lowering inflation with a lag of a year or more; it cannot undo a supply shock already in prices.

The FOMC's September 2026 statement says its quarter-point hike 'will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal'; this is the central bank asserting the mechanism, not evidence of it.
